The limiting equations have unique nondegenerate roots; implicit differentiation gives exactly Ystar and Yc, both positive. Therefore the expansions, O(\(\epsilon^2\)) remainder, sharp positive correction exponent and exact interfamily ratio follow for all fixed nu, not from finite experiments. value.rationale: The singular \(q\to0\) boundary is geometrically natural because the unscaled exponential radii diverge, and recently published exact root equations did not describe their rates. A single simultaneous theorem identifies three normalization-dependent leading radii for two analytically different q-Bessel constructions, supplies all twelve strictly positive first corrections and proves the sharp exponent dichotomy \(q^2\) versus q. An explicit asymptotic Jackson/Hahn--Exton radius ratio distinguishes their geometric scales. This is a nontrivial quantitative natural invariant for special-function geometry, not a redefinition or a finite-table recomputation; no arbitrary parameter slice is introduced except the necessary nu range for convexity factorization.
